rationale: An enumerator the analyzer cannot NAME must not be published from a macro invocation's ARGUMENTS. curl declares its option table with `#define CURLOPT(id, type, num) CURLOPT_##id = num` in enumerator position, which the pinned grammar reads as an enumerator_list of ERROR fragments (the macro's punctuation) with bare `enumerator(identifier)` fragments between them -- one per argument. The extractor read every enumerator as real, so each invocation published its ARGUMENTS as enum members: measured `CURLOPTTYPE_CBPOINT` twenty-one times under `CURLoption` in curl/include/curl/curl.h, with `CURLOPT_WRITEDATA` beside it and a `contains` edge onto each. The corpus consequence is visible as duplicate member names -- 41 in curl, 41 in libgit2, 19 in redis -- two phantoms per invocation colliding under one owner. The real name is derivable only AFTER token pasting, so it is C-D2 territory and silence is the honest result. The two controls are the readings a whole-list rejection would destroy, and they are the reason the rule is positional rather than a blunt 'this list is damaged': `PLAIN_MEMBER` sits BETWEEN two invocations in the same damaged list and is a clean enumerator, and `REAL_AFTER` follows one. The libgit2/redis duplicate members are the same class -- a tag redeclared in mutually exclusive preprocessor arms, plus these argument phantoms -- which is why duplicate member names are a REPORTED dimension and not a gate (see the gate's P8 note).
